title: The Makers of Modern China
author: Zheng Xiaoqiong
review: What a fantastic portrait of life and industrialization. This reminds of so much. It's just wonderfully rich and could be read to learn about almost anything.

title: Escape Artists: Romantasy at the End of the World
author: Daniel Yadin
review: This is the best thing I've ever read on this topic, and that is high praise given how much there is out there. It's like this is the only thing you need to read on this, really, and I guess it just took this long for someone to produce something worth reading on the subject. It's precise and considered, and both takes the subject matter seriously and does not do the kind of feel-good all things are valid thing that it critiques within. Some of the best lines in my opinion: 'Suffice it to say, for now, that the search is for a sexual impulse that has not had to pass through society on its way to your body. No heterofatalism here: just an innate, unmediated, innocent lust.' and ''We know Rebecca chooses every word intentioanlly and there are no accidents,' said one fan, who may as well have been describing God's writing of the Torah.' The second one is just really fantastic because it gets to a fundamental weirdness of this genre and its reception, which is that somehow its fandom-ness makes it so it is supposed to transgress a basic law of human creativity which is that not all things are on purpose, and that sometimes the author's interpretation is different than the reader's. It's just such an elegant and entertaining piece of writing. Gold standard!

title: What Did Men Do to Deserve This?
author: Jessica Winter
review: I don't understand why people are suggesting on Twitter that this is a novel take. I do not like writing like this. I don't understand why so much mainstream writing about men and masculinity is so massively ungenerous. Like, why does this author lay out all of the negative things facing men and then basically just go, 'but these are also affecting women, so who cares?'. Like, why can't we imagine that a genuine shift in gender relations (whether superficial or not) over the last century or so could have genuine significance? Obviously these right wing manosphere fascist hacks are what they are. But jeez. Don't some things really have an effect? Not everything is a sham. I didn't think this was good.
